title: Alexandra Park & Bowes Park
intro: Streets below the 'People's Palace', with one of the best views over London, a boating lake and woodland garden in its park, and Muswell Hill's Edwardian broadway up the hill.

items.name: Alexandra Palace
items.blurb: The great Victorian 'People's Palace' of 1873, where the BBC began the world's first regular high-definition television service in 1936.
items.tip: The theatre and the ice rink are inside; the terrace view is free.

items.name: The view from Alexandra Palace
items.blurb: From the terrace in front of the palace the whole of London is laid out below, from the City to Canary Wharf.
items.tip: Come at sunset, or on Bonfire Night for the fireworks.

items.name: Alexandra Park boating lake
items.blurb: A boating lake below the palace with pedalos in summer, a café and a playground.

items.name: Muswell Hill Broadway
items.blurb: An Edwardian shopping centre on the top of the hill, with parades of red-brick shops, cafés and an Art Deco cinema.
items.tip: Walk over from the palace along The Avenue.

items.name: Bounds Green station
items.blurb: A 1932 Piccadilly line station by Charles Holden with a brick and glass ticket hall, Grade II listed.
items.tip: The Piccadilly line runs from here to King's Cross in about 15 minutes.
